name: Zerubbabel
description: Governor living at the time of Exile and Return

points: The record runs on through the sons of Zerubbabel and their descendants, and these too are our forefathers, kept by name so we can search out our fathers.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: He sends them back by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer and numbers them to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: All these Sheshbazzar brings up with the captives that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem. The same account is recorded in 1 Esdras.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: The first wave came led by Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and the other chief men. Zerubbabel had been one of the bodyguards of the Persian Empire, the wisest guard granted a request in 1 Esdras.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

points: Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: In the second year of their coming, Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the remnant of their brethren the priests and Levites appoint the Levites from twenty years old and upward to set forward the work.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin hear of the building and come to Zerubbabel asking to build with them, claiming to seek the same God since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

points: But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us. What did they say unto them? You have what? Ye have nothing to do with us. That is like when I did the interview: can white people come join you all? No. No, they cannot join us. That simple. They were mad as hell. So can white people join? I am saying, you are saying all this, but can — no, no, no. Sorry. And they were mad. But that is what it is. That is what our forefathers did.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Zerubbabel and Jeshua answered, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build. Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

points: Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief of the fathers refuse them: the strangers have nothing to do with building the house of the God of Israel.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

points: After the work had been hindered for roughly two years, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stirred up the leaders, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose again to build the house of God.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: These are the priests and Levites that went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, and the rest named as the chiefs of the priests and their brethren in the days of Jeshua.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: In the second year of Darius the king came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, and to Joshua the high priest.

note.label: Haggai 1: Consider Your Ways

points: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, and the people did fear before the Lord.

Notice: Joshua was the high priest, Zerubbabel was the governor; Haggai was not in those positions. But Joshua and Zerubbabel humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord; they knew Haggai and Zechariah were sent of God. Zerubbabel could have said, arrest him, lock him up; or he could have punched a hole in his chest. He did none of that. He said, I recognize the word of the Lord; I am going to humble myself.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, and the spirit of Joshua, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: The word comes to Zerubbabel the governor of Judah, to Joshua the high priest, and to the residue of the people.

note.label: Haggai 2: The Glory of the Latter House

points: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: The Most High gave Haggai these prophecies to speak to Zerubbabel, showing him the things that are to come to pass.

note.label: Haggai 2: The Glory of the Latter House

points: In that day will I take thee, O Zerubbabel my servant, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts.

note.label: Haggai 2: The Glory of the Latter House

points: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel. Reading shown on screen: Zerubbabel means born in Babylon, or seed, offspring of Babylon; some scholars note it could also be understood as born in exile, but the standard rendering is born in Babylon. One of our forefathers was named Born in Babylon; that is today's lesson: we are born in Babylon.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts. Now you have to ask: why did the Lord say that to Zerubbabel?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts. Now we know why the Lord said that to Zerubbabel: he was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. He is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills, Zerubbabel; we know you can break bones, but that is not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what is going to do it.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Zerubbabel was a warrior, and he had it in his mind to take over. The Lord said no: this is not the time to fight. Now is the time to build your people, build your nation, build the temple.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

note.label: Zechariah 4: The Candlestick, the Two Olive Trees, and the Word to Zerubbabel

points: Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: the great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall be flattened.
And he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Who art thou, O great mountain? Remember, Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity; Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So this great mountain is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Does everybody understand that?

Before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: flattened, destroyed. And he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it. Why is he crying grace, grace? It said in Isaiah: because of the oppressors. This is showing you Zerubbabel is in these last days as well.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Who art thou, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain. The mountain is America.
Zerubbabel means born in Babylon; he rejoices to see the plummet in his hand with those seven, the angels of the last plagues.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

points: Who art thou, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.

note.label: Zechariah 4: The Candlestick, the Two Olive Trees, and the Word to Zerubbabel

points: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. However, this goes deeper than that: verses 6 through 9 are also going into the last days.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.

note.label: Zechariah 4: The Candlestick, the Two Olive Trees, and the Word to Zerubbabel

points: After they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel and Salathiel begat Zorobabel, both in captivity; a captive does not sit on the throne.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Zorobabel's line runs Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan, Jacob, and Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary; Joseph comes out of the kings, out of Solomon's kingdom.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah
